input.quote: Customer may terminate an Order Form immediately if Vendor suffers a material Security Incident, repeatedly misses a critical service level, violates Applicable Law in performing the Services, or infringes a third party's intellectual property and cannot provide the remedies required by Section 20.5.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no indemnification article at all: the outline jumps from Section 19 (Warranties) to Section 21 (Limitation of Liability), and searches for "indemnif", "defend" and "hold harmless" return only references that assume an indemnity exists (9.3 cross-references the remedies "required by Section 20.5"; 19.4 refers to "indemnified claims"; 21.3 treats "indemnification obligations" as Excluded Claims; 30.5 preserves "vested indemnity rights"). With no Vendor IP indemnity, the clause falls below even the fallback and into walk-away territory, and Section 9.3's cross-reference is broken. We inserted Section 20 with the preferred Vendor defence/indemnity for third-party IP infringement, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data breaches and gross negligence/wilful misconduct, plus customary exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies in 20.5 (restoring the cross-reference), standard claim procedure, and a narrow Customer indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

proposal.summary: Insert missing Section 20 (Indemnification) with Vendor IP/misconduct indemnity, narrow Customer indemnity, procedure and infringement remedies.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The indemnification article is missing even though Sections 9.3, 19.4, 21.3 and 30.5 assume it exists (9.3 cross-references Section 20.5). We have inserted our standard Vendor indemnity for third-party IP claims, breach of law, Vendor-caused data breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct, with usual exclusions, infringement remedies, standard procedure and a narrow Customer indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

ops.text: Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, losses, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services, Deliverables, or Vendor Technology infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of Applicable Law; (c) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

Vendor's obligation in Section 20.1(a) does not apply to the extent a claim arises from Customer's unauthorized modification of the Services or Deliverables, combination with items not supplied or recommended by Vendor where the claim would have been avoided absent the combination, or Vendor's compliance with written specifications supplied by Customer.

Customer shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Vendor from and against any third-party claim to the extent arising out of content or materials provided by Customer for use in the Services (other than to the extent the claim is covered by Section 20.1) or Customer's breach of Applicable Law.

The indemnified party shall give the indemnifying party prompt written notice of the claim (delay excuses the indemnifying party only to the extent it is materially prejudiced), allow the indemnifying party to control the defence with counsel of its choice, and provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying party's expense. The indemnified party may participate with its own counsel at its own cost. The indemnifying party shall not settle a claim in a way that imposes liability, an admission, or a non-monetary obligation on the indemnified party without its prior written consent.

If the Services or Deliverables are, or in Vendor's reasonable opinion are likely to become, the subject of an infringement claim, Vendor shall at its expense and Customer's option procure the right for Customer to continue using them, or modify or replace them with functionally equivalent, non-infringing items that meet the requirements of this Agreement. If neither option is reasonably available, Customer may terminate the affected Order Form and Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees for the terminated period and Fees paid for affected Deliverables.
